nodes.name: Duality pairing
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ be a reflexive real Banach space with norm $\|\cdot\|$ and let $\pair{\cdot}{\cdot}$ be the duality pairing between $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ and its topological dual $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*$.

nodes.name: Monotone and maximally monotone operator
nodes.statement: A set-valued operator $M\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to 2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}$ with graph $\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M=\menge{(x,x^*)\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\times\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}{x^*\in Mx}$ is monotone if \begin{equation} (\forall (x_1,x_1^*)\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M)(\forall (x_2,x_2^*)\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M)\quad \pair{x_1-x_2}{x_1^*-x_2^*}\ensuremath{\geqslant} 0, \end{equation} and maximally monotone if, furthermore, there exists no monotone operator from $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ to $2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}$ the graph of which properly contains $\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M$.
differentia: there exists no monotone operator from $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ to $2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}$ the graph of which properly contains $\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M$
nodes.statement_short: M is monotone if <x1-x2, x1*-x2*> >= 0 on its graph; maximally monotone if its graph has no proper monotone extension.

nodes.name: Coercive and supercoercive function
nodes.statement: Let $f\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}$. Then $f$ is coercive if $\lim_{\|x\|\to+\infty}f(x)=+\infty$ and supercoercive if $\lim_{\|x\|\to+\infty}f(x)/\|x\|=+\infty$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: \ref{pvb8uh4504i}: Since $f$ and $g$ are Legendre functions, so are $f^*$ and $g^*$ \cite[Corollary~5.5]{Ccm01}. Therefore, it follows from \cite[Theorem~5.6(iii)]{Ccm01} that $\partial f$ and $\partial g^*$ are single-valued on $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial f=\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} f$ and $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial g^*=\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} g^*$, respectively. On the other hand, we derive from \eqref{epOlk28ha14} that $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}=\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} f\times\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} g^*$ and that \begin{equation} \partial\boldsymbol{f}\colon\boldsymbol{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}}\to 2^{\boldsymbol{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}}\colon (x,y^*)\mapsto \partial f(x)\times\partial g^*(y^*). \end{equation} Thus, $\partial\boldsymbol{f}$ is single-valued on \begin{equation} \ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial\boldsymbol{f}=\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial f\times\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial g^* =\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} f\times\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} g^*=\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}(\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} f\times\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} g^*) =\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}. \end{equation} Likewise, since \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{f}^*\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}\colon (x^*,y)\mapsto f^*(x^*)+g(y), \end{equation} we deduce that $\partial\boldsymbol{f}^*$ is single-valued on $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial\boldsymbol{f}^*=\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}^*$. Consequently, \cite[Theorems~5.4 and~5.6]{Ccm01} assert that $\boldsymbol{f}$ is a Legendre function. \ref{pvb8uh4504ii}: It follows from Proposition~\ref{ppOlk28ha12}\ref{ppOlk28ha12ia} that $\boldsymbol{Z}$ is a closed convex subset of $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$. Hence, since $\boldsymbol{Z}\cap\text{\rm int\,dom}\,\boldsymbol{f}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$, we derive from \ref{pvb8uh4504i} and \cite[Corollary~7.9]{Ccm01} that $(\overline{x},\overline{y}^*)=P^{\boldsymbol{f}}_{\boldsymbol{Z}} (x_0,y_0^*)$ is uniquely defined.
nodes.statement_short: Separable structure gives single-valued subdifferentials of f and f*, hence Legendre; existence and uniqueness via Bregman projector theory.

nodes.name: Bregman half-space H^f and Haugazeau-type operator Q^f
nodes.statement_short: H^f(x,y) is the half-space onto which y is the Bregman projection of x; Q^f(x0,x,y) is the Bregman projection of x0 onto H^f(x0,x) cap H^f(x,y).
nodes.label: d:B-haugazeau

nodes.name: Closure of intersection with interior
nodes.statement: {\rm\cite[Lemma~3.2]{Sico03}} Let $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$ be a reflexive real Banach space, and let $\boldsymbol{C}_1$ and $\boldsymbol{C}_2$ be convex subsets of $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$ such that $\boldsymbol{C}_1$ is closed and $\boldsymbol{C}_1\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\boldsymbol{C}_2\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$. Then $\overline{\boldsymbol{C}_1\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\boldsymbol{C}}_2= \boldsymbol{C}_1\cap\overline{\boldsymbol{C}}_2$.
assumptions: Let $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$ be a reflexive real Banach space, and let $\boldsymbol{C}_1$ and $\boldsymbol{C}_2$ be convex subsets of $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$ such that $\boldsymbol{C}_1$ is closed and $\boldsymbol{C}_1\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\boldsymbol{C}_2\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$.
nodes.label: l:2002

nodes.name: Bregman-Haugazeau best approximation scheme
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$ be a reflexive real Banach space, let $\boldsymbol{f}\in\Gamma_0(\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}})$ be a Legendre function, let $\boldsymbol{C}$ be a closed convex subset of $\overline{\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}}\boldsymbol{f}$ such that $\boldsymbol{C}\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$, let $\boldsymbol{x}_0\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}$, and set $\overline{\boldsymbol{x}}=P_{\boldsymbol{C}}^{\boldsymbol{f}} \boldsymbol{x}_0$. At every iteration $n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}$, find $\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}$ such that $\boldsymbol{C}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})$ and set \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{x}_{n+1}=Q^{\boldsymbol{f}} \big(\boldsymbol{x}_0,\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}\big). \end{equation} Then the following hold: \begin{enumerate} \item $(\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})$ $\boldsymbol{C}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_0,\boldsymbol{x}_n)$. \item $(\boldsymbol{x}_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$ is a well-defined bounded sequence in $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}$. \item Suppose that, for some $n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}$, $\boldsymbol{x}_n\in\boldsymbol{C}$. Then $(\forall k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})$ $\boldsymbol{x}_{n+k}=\overline{\boldsymbol{x}}$. \item $\sum_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1}, \boldsymbol{x}_n)<+\infty$. \item $(\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})$ $D^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2},\boldsymbol{x}_n)\ensuremath{\leqslant} D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1},\boldsymbol{x}_n)$. \item $\sum_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}, \boldsymbol{x}_n)<+\infty$. \item $[\,\boldsymbol{x}_n\ensuremath{\:\rightharpoonup\:}\overline{\boldsymbol{x}}$ and $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_n)\to\boldsymbol{f} (\overline{\boldsymbol{x}})\,]$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n, \overline{\boldsymbol{x}})\to 0$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $\ensuremath{{\mathfrak W}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\subset\boldsymbol{C}$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: let $\boldsymbol{C}$ be a closed convex subset of $\overline{\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}}\boldsymbol{f}$ such that $\boldsymbol{C}\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$
find $\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}$ such that $\boldsymbol{C}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})$
conclusions: $(\boldsymbol{x}_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$ is a well-defined bounded sequence in $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}$.
nodes.statement_short: Haugazeau-type Bregman outer-approximation iteration: iterates are bounded, increments are summable, and strong Bregman convergence to P_C^f x_0 iff weak cluster points lie in C.
nodes.label: p:2

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.5
nodes.statement: Item~\ref{p:2i-} is found in \cite[Proof of Proposition~3.3]{Pams03}. The first equivalence in \ref{p:2iv} follows from \cite[Propositions~2.2(ii)]{Pams03}. To establish the remaining assertions, set \begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad T_n= P_{H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})}^{\boldsymbol{f}}. \end{equation} Then, for every $n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}$, Definition~\ref{d:B-haugazeau} yields $T_n\boldsymbol{x}_n=\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}$, \cite[Proposition~3.32(ii)(b)]{Sico03} yields $\ensuremath{\text{\rm Fix}\,} T_n=H^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}) \cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\:dom}\boldsymbol{f}}$, and we derive from Lemma~\ref{l:2002} that \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{C}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}) \cap\overline{\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}}\boldsymbol{f}= \overline{H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\:dom}\boldsymbol{f}}} =\overline{\ensuremath{\text{\rm Fix}\,}}T_n. \end{equation} On the other hand, \begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}\neq \boldsymbol{C}\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} \boldsymbol{f}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}) \cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}=\ensuremath{\text{\rm Fix}\,} T_n \end{equation} and, therefore, $\bigcap_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\ensuremath{\text{\rm Fix}\,} T_n\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$. Altogether, \cite[Condition~3.2]{Pams03} is satisfied and it follows from \cite[Propositions~3.3 and 3.4]{Pams03} and \cite[Proof of Proposition~3.4(vii)]{Pams03} that the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Cast the iteration as Bregman projections T_n with C contained in the closure of Fix T_n, then invoke the results of Bauschke-Combettes (2003).

nodes.name: Coercive and bounded set-valued operator
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ be a reflexive real Banach space such that $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\neq\{0\}$ and let $M\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to 2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}$. Then $M$ is \emph{coercive} if \begin{equation} (\ensuremath{\exists\,} z\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M)\quad \lim_{\|x\|\to+\infty}\inf\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{Mx}}{\|x\|}=\ensuremath{{+\infty}}, \end{equation} and it is \emph{bounded} if it maps bounded sets to bounded set.
nodes.section: 2.3 Coercivity and boundedness of monotone operators

nodes.name: Sufficient conditions for coercivity
nodes.statement: Let $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ be a reflexive real Banach space such that $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\neq\{0\}$ and let $M\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to 2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}$. Suppose that one of the following holds: \begin{enumerate} \item $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M$ is nonempty and bounded. \item $M$ is uniformly monotone at some point $z\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M$ with a supercoercive modulus: there exists a strictly increasing function $\phi\colon\left[0,+\infty\right[\to\left[0,+\infty\right]$ that vanishes only at $0$ such that $\lim\limits_{t\to+\infty}\phi(t)/t=+\infty$ and \begin{equation} (\forall (x,x^*)\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M)(\forall z^*\in Mz)\quad \pair{x-z}{x^*-z^*}\ensuremath{\geqslant}\phi(\|x-z\|). \end{equation} \item $M=\partial\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is a supercoercive function in $\Gamma_0(\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})$. \end{enumerate} Then $M$ is coercive.

nodes.name: Explicitly computable Bregman resolvent for a non-subdifferential operator
nodes.statement:
The implementation of algorithm \eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h} requires the evaluation of the operator $(
abla h+A)^{-1}$. We provide a simple example in the Euclidean plane $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ of a maximally monotone operator $A$ for which $(
abla h+A)^{-1}$ can be computed explicitly, whereas the classical resolvent $(\ensuremath{\operatorname{Id}}\,+A)^{-1}$ is difficult to evaluate. Let $ eta\in\ensuremath{\left]0,+\inftyight[}$ and let $\psi\colon\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}	o\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ be a Legendre function with a $ eta$ Lipschitz-continuous derivative. Set  egin{equation} A\colon\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^2	o\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^2\colon (\xi_1,\xi_2)\mapsto  ig( eta\xi_1-\psi'(\xi_1)-\xi_2, \xi_1+ eta\xi_2-\psi'(\xi_2) ig) \end{equation} and  egin{equation} h\colon\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^2	o\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\inftyight]}\colon (\xi_1,\xi_2)\mapsto \psi(\xi_1)+\psi(\xi_2). \end{equation} Then it follows from \cite[Theorem~18.15]{Livre1} that $A$ is the sum of the gradient of the convex function $(\xi_1,\xi_2)\mapsto eta\xi_1^2/2-\psi(\xi_1)+  eta\xi_2^2/2-\psi(\xi_2)$ and of the skew linear operator $(\xi_1,\xi_2)\mapsto(-\xi_2,\xi_1)$. Thus, $A$ is a maximally monotone operator \cite[Corollary~24.4]{Livre1} which is not the subdifferential of a convex function. In addition, as in Proposition~ef{pvb8uh4504}ef{pvb8uh4504i}, $h$ is a Legendre function and  egin{equation}  ig( orall (\xi_1,\xi_2)\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^2 ig)\quad (
abla h+A)^{-1}(\xi_1,\xi_2) =\Bigg(\dfrac{ eta\xi_1+\xi_2}{1+ eta^2}, \dfrac{ eta\xi_2-\xi_1}{1+ eta^2}\Bigg). \end{equation}

Consider the primal problem \begin{equation} \minimize{x_1\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}_1,\ldots,\,x_m\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}_m}{\sum_{i=1}^m \varphi_i(x_i)+\sum_{k=1}^p \psi_k\bigg(\sum_{i=1}^mL_{ki}x_i\bigg)}, \end{equation} the dual problem \begin{equation} \minimize{y^*_1\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}_1^*,\ldots,\,y^*_p\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}_p^*}{\sum_{i=1}^m \varphi_i^*\bigg(-\sum_{k=1}^pL_{ki}^*y^*_k\bigg) +\sum_{k=1}^p\psi^*_k(y^*_k)}, \end{equation} and let \begin{multline} \boldsymbol{Z}=\bigg\{({x},{y}^*) \in\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}\;\bigg |\; (\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,m\})\;\;-\sum_{k=1}^pL_{ki}^*y_k^* \in\partial\varphi_i(x_i)\:\;\text{and}\\ (\forall k\in\{1,\ldots,p\})\;\;\sum_{i=1}^mL_{ki}x_i\in \partial\psi_k^*(y_k^*)\bigg\} \end{multline} be the associated Kuhn-Tucker set. For every $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$, let $f_i\in\Gamma_0(\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}_i)$ be a Legendre function and let $x_{i,0}\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} f_i$. For every $k\in\{1,\ldots,p\}$, let $g_k\in\Gamma_0(\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}_k)$ be a Legendre function and let $y^*_{k,0}\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} g^*_k$. Set ${x}_0=(x_{i,0})_{1\ensuremath{\leqslant} i\ensuremath{\leqslant} m}$, ${y}_0^*=(y_{k,0}^*)_{1\ensuremath{\leqslant} k\ensuremath{\leqslant} p}$, and \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{f}\colon\boldsymbol{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}}\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}\colon ({x},{y}^*)\mapsto \sum_{i=1}^mf_i(x_i)+\sum_{k=1}^pg_k^*(y_k^*), \end{equation} and suppose that $\boldsymbol{Z}\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$. The objective is to find the best Bregman approximation $\big((\overline{x}_i)_{1\ensuremath{\leqslant} i\ensuremath{\leqslant} m}, (\overline{y}_k^*)_{1\ensuremath{\leqslant} k\ensuremath{\leqslant} p}\big) =P_{\boldsymbol{Z}}^{\boldsymbol{f}} ({x}_0,{y}_0^*)$ to $({x}_0,{y}_0^*)$ from $\boldsymbol{Z}$.

nodes.name: Introduce M and S
nodes.statement: Set $\boldsymbol{M}\colon\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}\to 2^{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}^*}\colon(x,y^*)\mapsto Ax\times B^{-1}y^*$ and $\boldsymbol{S}\colon\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}} \to\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}^*\colon (x,y^*)\mapsto (L^*y^*,-Lx)$. Since $A$ and $B^{-1}$ are maximally monotone, so is $\boldsymbol{M}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce M = A x B^{-1} and the skew operator S; M is maximally monotone.

nodes.name: M+S maximally monotone
nodes.statement: On the other hand, $\boldsymbol{S}$ is linear, bounded, and positive since \begin{equation} (\forall(x,y^*)\in\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}})\quad \pair{\boldsymbol{S}(x,y^*)}{(x,y^*)}= \pair{x}{L^*y^*}+\pair{-Lx}{y^*}=0. \end{equation} Thus, it follows from \cite[Section~17]{Simo08} that $\boldsymbol{S}$ is maximally monotone with $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\boldsymbol{S}=\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$. In turn, we derive from \cite[Theorem~24.1(a)]{Simo08} that \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S}\;\text{is maximally monotone.} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: S is skew hence maximally monotone; sum M+S is maximally monotone (Simons).

nodes.name: Item (i)(a)
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12ia}: Let $(x,y^*)\in\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$. Then \begin{eqnarray} \boldsymbol{0}\in\boldsymbol{M}(x,y^*)+\boldsymbol{S}(x,y^*) &\Leftrightarrow& 0\in Ax+L^*y^*\quad\text{and}\quad 0\in B^{-1}y^*-Lx\nonumber\\ &\Leftrightarrow& -L^*y^*\in Ax \quad\text{and}\quad Lx\in B^{-1}y^*\nonumber\\ &\Leftrightarrow& (x,y^*)\in \boldsymbol{Z}. \end{eqnarray} Therefore, we derive from \eqref{egVxZ5y820} and \cite[Lemma~1.1(a)]{IVBro65} that $\boldsymbol{Z}=\ensuremath{\text{\rm zer}\,}(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})= (\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})^{-1}(0)$ is closed and convex.
nodes.statement_short: Z = zer(M+S), hence closed and convex.

nodes.name: Item (i)(b)
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12ib}: Let $x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$. Then $x\in\mathscr{P}\Leftrightarrow 0\in Ax+L^*BLx\Leftrightarrow (\ensuremath{\exists\,} y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*)\; [-L^*y^*\in Ax\;\text{and}\;y^*\in BLx] \Leftrightarrow (\ensuremath{\exists\,} y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*)\;(x,y^*) \in\boldsymbol{Z}$. Hence $\mathscr{P}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{Z}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$. Likewise, let $y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*$. Then $y^*\in\mathscr{D}\Leftrightarrow 0\in-LA^{-1}(-L^*y^*)+B^{-1}y^* \Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\; [x\in A^{-1}(-L^*y^*)\;\text{and}\;0\in-Lx+B^{-1}y^*] \Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\; [-L^*y^*\in Ax\;\text{and}\; Lx\in B^{-1}y^*] \Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\;(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Chains of equivalences identify primal and dual solutions with projections of Z.

nodes.name: Item (i)(c)
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from (i)(b).

nodes.name: Item (ii)(a)
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12iia} : Let $\mathsf{a}\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} A$ and $\mathsf{b}\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} B$. Then $\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$ $\Rightarrow$ [$-L^*b^*=a^*\in Aa$ and $La=b\in B^{-1}b^*$] $\Rightarrow$ $(a,b^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$. In addition, \begin{multline} \boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0} \quad\Rightarrow\quad \eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\pair{a}{a^*} +\pair{b}{b^*}=\pair{a}{-L^*b^*}+\pair{La}{b^*}\\ =-\pair{La}{b^*}+\pair{La}{b^*}=0. \end{multline} Thus $\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$. Conversely, $\boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: s*=0 gives (a,b*) in Z and eta=0, equivalently H = whole space.

nodes.name: Item (ii)(b)
nodes.statement_short: Prove both inclusions between Z and the intersection of the half-spaces.

nodes.name: Intersection inside Z
nodes.statement_short: Maximal monotonicity of M+S places points of the intersection in Z.

nodes.name: Z inside each half-space
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of A and B bounds <x,s*> by eta.

nodes.name: Item (iii)
nodes.statement: \ref{ppOlk28ha12iii}: Set $(\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})$ $\boldsymbol{x}_n=(a_n,b_n^*)$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_n^*=(a_n^*+L^*b_n^*,b_n-La_n)$. Then $\boldsymbol{x}_n\ensuremath{\:\rightharpoonup\:} (x,y^*)$, $\boldsymbol{x}_n^*\to \boldsymbol{0}$, and $(\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})$ $(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_n^*)\in \ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,}(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$. However, it follows from \eqref{egVxZ5y820} that $\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,}(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$ is sequentially closed in $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}^{\text{weak}}\times\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}^{*\text{strong}}$ \cite[Lemma~1.2]{IVBro65}. Hence, $\boldsymbol{0}\in(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})(x,y^*)$, i.e., by \eqref{egVxZ5y828}, $(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weak-strong sequential closedness of gra(M+S) (Browder) gives the limit in Z.

nodes.name: Item (i)
nodes.statement: \ref{pvb8uh4504i}: Since $f$ and $g$ are Legendre functions, so are $f^*$ and $g^*$ \cite[Corollary~5.5]{Ccm01}. Therefore, it follows from \cite[Theorem~5.6(iii)]{Ccm01} that $\partial f$ and $\partial g^*$ are single-valued on $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial f=\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} f$ and $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial g^*=\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} g^*$, respectively. On the other hand, we derive from \eqref{epOlk28ha14} that $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}=\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} f\times\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} g^*$ and that \begin{equation} \partial\boldsymbol{f}\colon\boldsymbol{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}}\to 2^{\boldsymbol{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}}\colon (x,y^*)\mapsto \partial f(x)\times\partial g^*(y^*). \end{equation} Thus, $\partial\boldsymbol{f}$ is single-valued on \begin{equation} \ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial\boldsymbol{f}=\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial f\times\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial g^* =\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} f\times\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} g^*=\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}(\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} f\times\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} g^*) =\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}. \end{equation} Likewise, since \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{f}^*\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}\colon (x^*,y)\mapsto f^*(x^*)+g(y), \end{equation} we deduce that $\partial\boldsymbol{f}^*$ is single-valued on $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\partial\boldsymbol{f}^*=\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}^*$. Consequently, \cite[Theorems~5.4 and~5.6]{Ccm01} assert that $\boldsymbol{f}$ is a Legendre function.
nodes.statement_short: Separable subdifferentials of f and f* are single-valued on interiors, so f is Legendre.

nodes.name: Item (ii)
nodes.statement: \ref{pvb8uh4504ii}: It follows from Proposition~\ref{ppOlk28ha12}\ref{ppOlk28ha12ia} that $\boldsymbol{Z}$ is a closed convex subset of $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$. Hence, since $\boldsymbol{Z}\cap\text{\rm int\,dom}\,\boldsymbol{f}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$, we derive from \ref{pvb8uh4504i} and \cite[Corollary~7.9]{Ccm01} that $(\overline{x},\overline{y}^*)=P^{\boldsymbol{f}}_{\boldsymbol{Z}} (x_0,y_0^*)$ is uniquely defined.
nodes.statement_short: Z closed convex and meets int dom f, so the Bregman projection exists uniquely.

nodes.statement: To establish the remaining assertions, set \begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad T_n= P_{H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})}^{\boldsymbol{f}}. \end{equation}

nodes.statement: Then, for every $n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}$, Definition~\ref{d:B-haugazeau} yields $T_n\boldsymbol{x}_n=\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}$, \cite[Proposition~3.32(ii)(b)]{Sico03} yields $\ensuremath{\text{\rm Fix}\,} T_n=H^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}) \cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\:dom}\boldsymbol{f}}$, and we derive from Lemma~\ref{l:2002} that \begin{equation} \boldsymbol{C}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}) \cap\overline{\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}}\boldsymbol{f}= \overline{H^{\boldsymbol{f}} (\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\:dom}\boldsymbol{f}}} =\overline{\ensuremath{\text{\rm Fix}\,}}T_n. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Common fixed points
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}\neq \boldsymbol{C}\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} \boldsymbol{f}\subset H^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}) \cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}=\ensuremath{\text{\rm Fix}\,} T_n \end{equation} and, therefore, $\bigcap_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\ensuremath{\text{\rm Fix}\,} T_n\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$.
nodes.statement_short: The fixed-point sets have nonempty intersection.

nodes.statement: Altogether, \cite[Condition~3.2]{Pams03} is satisfied and it follows from \cite[Propositions~3.3 and 3.4]{Pams03} and \cite[Proof of Proposition~3.4(vii)]{Pams03} that the proof is complete.

nodes.name: Case (i)
nodes.statement: \ref{l:20i}: Let $x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ and let $z\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M$. Then, if $\|x\|$ is sufficiently large, we have $Mx=\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$ and therefore $\inf{\pair{x-z}{Mx}}/{\|x\|}=\ensuremath{{+\infty}}$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Coercivity and boundedness of monotone operators
nodes.statement_short: Mx is empty for large x, so the quotient is +infinity.

nodes.name: Case (ii)
nodes.statement: \ref{l:20ii}: We have \begin{equation} (\forall (x,x^*)\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M)(\forall z^*\in Mz)\quad \pair{x-z}{x^*-z^*}\ensuremath{\geqslant}\phi(\|x-z\|). \end{equation} Hence, for every $x\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M$ such that $\|x\|>\|z\|$, we have \begin{align} (\forall x^*\in Mx)(\forall z^*\in Mz)\quad \dfrac{\pair{x-z}{x^*}}{\|x\|} &\ensuremath{\geqslant}\dfrac{\phi(\|x-z\|)-\|x-z\|\,\|z^*\|}{\|x\|}\nonumber\\ &=\dfrac{\|x-z\|}{\|x\|}\bigg( \dfrac{\phi(\|x-z\|)}{\|x-z\|}-\|z^*\|\bigg). \end{align} Thus, \begin{equation} \lim_{\|x\|\to+\infty}\inf\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{Mx}}{\|x\|}=\ensuremath{{+\infty}}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.3 Coercivity and boundedness of monotone operators
nodes.statement_short: Uniform monotonicity with supercoercive modulus bounds the quotient from below.

nodes.name: Case (iii)
nodes.statement: \ref{l:20iii}: In view of \ref{l:20i}, we suppose that $\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M$ is unbounded. Let $z\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M$. Then we derive from \eqref{e:subdiff} that, for every $x\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M\smallsetminus\{0\}$, \begin{equation} (\forall x^*\in Mx)\quad\dfrac{\varphi(x)-\varphi(z)}{\|x\|}\ensuremath{\leqslant} \dfrac{\pair{x-z}{x^*}}{\|x\|}. \end{equation} Hence, the supercoercivity of $\varphi$ yields \begin{equation} \lim_{\|x\|\to+\infty}\inf\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{Mx}}{\|x\|}=\ensuremath{{+\infty}} \end{equation} and $M$ is therefore coercive.
nodes.section: 2.3 Coercivity and boundedness of monotone operators
nodes.statement_short: Subgradient inequality plus supercoercivity of varphi.

nodes.name: Decompose elements
nodes.statement: Suppose that $x\in(\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M_1\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} M_2)\smallsetminus\{0\}$, let $x^*\in(M_1+M_2)x$, and let $z^*\in(M_1+M_2)z$. Then there exist $x_1^*\in M_1x$, $x_2^*\in M_2x$, $z_1^*\in M_1z$, and $z_2^*\in M_2z$ such that $x^*=x_1^*+x_2^*$ and $z^*=z_1^*+z_2^*$.

nodes.statement_short: Split x* and z* into M1 and M2 parts.

nodes.name: Bound and conclude
nodes.statement: In turn, the monotonicity of $M_2$ yields \begin{align} \dfrac{\pair{x-z}{x^*}}{\|x\|} &=\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{x_1^*-z_1^*}}{\|x\|} +\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{x_2^*-z_2^*}}{\|x\|} +\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{z^*}}{\|x\|}\nonumber\\ &\ensuremath{\geqslant}\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{x_1^*}}{\|x\|} +\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{z_2^*}}{\|x\|}\nonumber\\ &\ensuremath{\geqslant}\dfrac{\pair{x-z}{x_1^*}-\|x-z\|\,\|z_2^*\|}{\|x\|} \end{align} and \eqref{e:M1} implies that $M_1+M_2$ is coercive.
nodes.section: 2.3 Coercivity and boundedness of monotone operators
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of M2 gives a lower bound by the M1 quotient, which diverges.

nodes.name: Introduce bounds and decomposition
nodes.statement: Set $\beta=\sup_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\|x_n^*\|$ and $\sigma=\sup_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\gamma_n$. It follows from \eqref{eKKnhf74g12a} that, for every $n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}$, there exist $a_n^*\in M_1x_n$ and $b_n^*\in M_2x_n$ such that $x_n^*=a_n^*+\gamma_n b_n^*$.

Therefore, \eqref{eKKnhf74g13b} yields \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\ensuremath{{+\infty}}} \dfrac{\pair{x_{k_n}-z}{a^*_{k_n}}}{\|x_{k_n}\|}=\ensuremath{{+\infty}}. \end{equation}

Then $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*$ is the vector product space $\ensuremath{\raisebox{-0.5mm}{\mbox{\huge{$\times$}}}}_{\!\!i=1}^{\!\!m}\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}_i^*$ equipped with the norm $x^*\mapsto\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i^*\|^2}$ and $\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*$ is the vector product space $\ensuremath{\raisebox{-0.5mm}{\mbox{\huge{$\times$}}}}_{\!\!k=1}^{\!\!p}\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}_k^*$ equipped with the norm $y^*\mapsto\sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^p\|y_k^*\|^2}$. Let us introduce the operators \begin{equation} \begin{cases} A\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to 2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}\colon x\mapsto \ensuremath{\raisebox{-0.5mm}{\mbox{\huge{$\times$}}}}_{\!\!i=1}^{\!\!m}\partial\varphi_i(x_i)\\ B\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}\to 2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*}\colon y \mapsto\ensuremath{\raisebox{-0.5mm}{\mbox{\huge{$\times$}}}}_{\!\!k=1}^{\!\!p}\partial\psi_k(y_k)\\ L\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}\colon x\mapsto \big(\sum_{i=1}^mL_{ki}x_i\big)_{1\ensuremath{\leqslant} k\ensuremath{\leqslant} p} \end{cases} \end{equation} and the functions \begin{equation} \begin{cases} f\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}\colon x\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^mf_i(x_i)\\ h\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}\colon x\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^mh_i(x_i)\\ \varphi\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}\colon x\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^m\varphi_i(x_i)\\ g\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}\colon y\mapsto\sum_{k=1}^pg_k(y_k)\\ j\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}\to\ensuremath{\left]-\infty,+\infty\right]}\colon y\mapsto\sum_{k=1}^pj_k(y_k). \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the product spaces, A, B, L and the separable functions f, h, varphi, g, j.
